cls: Erythropoiesis-stimulating agent (ESA), recombinant long-acting erythropoietin analogue
pharm: Stimulates red blood cell production via erythropoietin receptors; longer half-life than epoetin alfa
quick: CKD: 0.45 mcg/kg IV/SC weekly; cancer: 2.25 mcg/kg SC weekly
Used in CKD anemia; IV preferred in hemodialysis
Hgb, BP, iron studies, thrombosis, seizures
summary: Darbepoetin alfa (Aranesp) is a long-acting erythropoiesis-stimulating agent used to treat anemia due to chronic kidney disease and anemia from myelosuppressive chemotherapy. It carries a boxed warning: ESAs increase the risk of death, myocardial infarction, stroke, venous thromboembolism, thrombosis of vascular access, and tumor progression or recurrence. Use the lowest dose sufficient to avoid red blood cell transfusion, do not target hemoglobin above 11 g/dL in CKD, and ensure adequate iron stores. In cancer, use only for chemotherapy-induced anemia where cure is not the anticipated outcome.
indications: Anemia due to chronic kidney disease (CKD) - dialysis and non-dialysis patients
Anemia due to concomitant myelosuppressive chemotherapy (with >=2 additional months of planned chemo)

dosage.d: 0.45 mcg/kg weekly OR 0.75 mcg/kg every 2 weeks

dosage.n: May also use 0.75 mcg/kg every 2 weeks
Non-dialysis may start 0.75 mcg/kg every 2 weeks

dosage.d: 2.25 mcg/kg weekly OR 500 mcg every 3 weeks

dosage.n: Do not exceed Hgb 11 g/dL (CKD); use lowest effective dose

admin: Administer IV or SC; do not shake (may denature/inactivate)
Evaluate and maintain iron status; supplement iron if needed
For hemodialysis patients, IV route is recommended
Use lowest dose sufficient to reduce need for RBC transfusions; do not exceed target Hgb 11 g/dL in CKD
moa: Stimulates erythropoiesis by the same mechanism as endogenous erythropoietin - binds and activates the erythropoietin receptor on erythroid progenitor cells, promoting proliferation and differentiation into mature red blood cells. Increased glycosylation gives a longer half-life than epoetin alfa.

absolute: Pure red cell aplasia (PRCA) that begins after treatment with darbepoetin or other erythropoietin protein drugs
Serious allergic reactions to darbepoetin alfa
relative: Active or recent malignancy (tumor progression risk)
monitor: Hemoglobin (do not exceed 11 g/dL in CKD)

preg: Limited data are insufficient to determine a drug-associated risk; animal studies showed increased early post-implantation loss near clinical starting doses. Weigh maternal benefits and fetal risks.
lact: No data on presence in human milk; as a large glycoprotein, significant transfer/oral absorption by the infant is unlikely. Consider maternal need and infant risk.
renal: Primary use is CKD-associated anemia; effective in both dialysis and non-dialysis patients. Intravenous administration is recommended for patients on hemodialysis.
hepatic: No specific dosage adjustment for hepatic impairment is established; use with general caution.

moderate: Other agents increasing thrombosis risk - additive thromboembolic risk
minor: Iron deficiency or therapy - inadequate iron blunts response; iron supplementation enhances response
interactions.diagnostics: Increases hemoglobin/hematocrit and reticulocyte count; monitor iron indices

serious: Thromboembolic events (MI, stroke, DVT/PE, vascular access thrombosis)

monitoring: Blood pressure before and during treatment
Response (avoid rapid Hgb rise >1 g/dL in 2 weeks)
counsel: Anemia improvement may take 2-6 weeks - not an immediate effect
Report chest pain, shortness of breath, leg swelling, weakness, or slurred speech
Blood pressure must be controlled; report severe headache
Iron supplementation is usually needed for the drug to work
If you have cancer, this drug is used only during chemotherapy
pk: Reticulocyte rise in days; Hgb rise ~2-6 weeks
IV ~21 h; SC ~49 h (longer than epoetin)
Refrigerate 2-8 C; do not freeze or shake; protect from light
pearls: Longer half-life than epoetin alfa allows less frequent dosing
Boxed warning: increased mortality, thrombosis, and tumor progression - use lowest effective dose, avoid Hgb >11 g/dL in CKD
Always correct iron deficiency before/while treating - hyporesponsiveness often reflects iron deficiency, infection, or inflammation
In cancer, avoid when the anticipated chemotherapy outcome is cure; discontinue after chemotherapy course
missed: If a scheduled dose is missed, administer as soon as possible and resume the regular dosing schedule; do not give two doses close together. Contact the prescriber for rescheduling guidance.
overdose: Excessive dosing causes polycythemia with risk of hypertension, headache, and thrombotic events. Management: hold therapy, monitor hemoglobin, manage hypertension; phlebotomy may be considered if clinically indicated.
